content.value_statement: Pricing decisions are hard when customer value, packaging, and conversion data are scattered. This skill turns research, metrics, and tier design into practical pricing recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Guides value-based pricing decisions using perceived value, alternatives, and cost floors.
Explains Van Westendorp, MaxDiff, Gabor-Granger, and conjoint research methods.
Helps choose value metrics such as seats, usage, records, transactions, or flat fees.
Designs good-better-best tiers with feature gates, usage limits, and support levels.
Compares freemium, free trial, reverse trial, and hybrid monetization models.
Plans price increases, pricing page structure, enterprise tiers, and price tests.
limitations: Does not run surveys, statistical models, or pricing page experiments by itself.
Requires accurate customer, competitor, conversion, churn, and revenue data from the user.
Provides strategy guidance, not legal advice for regional pricing or A/B testing rules.
Recommendations should be validated with customers before major pricing changes.

use_cases.title: Launch New SaaS Pricing
use_cases.description: Create initial tiers, value metrics, and price ranges before a product launch.

use_cases.title: Improve Packaging Conversion
use_cases.description: Restructure plans when users are confused, upgrades are weak, or tiers do not match value.

use_cases.title: Plan an Enterprise Motion
use_cases.description: Add custom pricing, support levels, contracts, and enterprise-ready packaging.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Current Pricing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current pricing. My product is [product], target market is [market], current tiers are [tiers], and my goal is [goal]. Identify the biggest issues and simple improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Value Metric
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a value metric for [product]. Customers get value from [outcomes], usage patterns are [usage], and current pricing is [pricing]. Compare the best options.

prompt_templates.title: Design Pricing Tiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Design good-better-best pricing tiers for [product]. Use these personas, features, limits, support needs, and willingness-to-pay signals: [details]. Explain each tier.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Price Increase
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a price increase plan for [product]. Current prices are [current], proposed prices are [new], customer segments are [segments], and risks are [risks]. Include communication and measurement steps.

output_examples.input: A team asks whether to use freemium or a free trial for a B2B SaaS onboarding tool.
output_examples.output: The skill compares activation time, marginal support cost, buying process, and upgrade triggers. It recommends a time-limited trial if setup effort and sales involvement are high.

output_examples.input: A founder shares three proposed tiers for a project management product.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies weak tier separation, suggests a per-seat value metric, moves integrations into higher tiers, and adds validation questions for customer interviews.

output_examples.input: A revenue leader wants to raise prices for existing customers.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines grandfathering, delayed rollout, annual lock-in options, customer messaging, and metrics to watch after the change.

best_practices: Bring current pricing, customer segments, conversion rates, churn, and competitor context before asking for recommendations.
Validate price points with willingness-to-pay research and customer conversations before changing published pricing.
Measure pricing changes with conversion, ARPU, LTV, churn, expansion, and segment-level performance.
anti_patterns: Choosing prices only from internal costs without estimating customer value and alternatives.
Creating many tiers or feature gates that make buying decisions harder.
Running pricing tests that create unfair customer experiences or damage trust.

faq.question: Can this skill recommend exact prices?
faq.answer: It can suggest price ranges and hypotheses. Exact prices should be validated with customer research and market data.

faq.question: Does it support SaaS pricing only?
faq.answer: It focuses on SaaS, but many frameworks also help marketplaces, services, and usage-based products.

faq.question: Can it design pricing surveys?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Van Westendorp, MaxDiff, Gabor-Granger, conjoint research, and related survey questions.

faq.question: Can it help with freemium decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares freemium, free trials, reverse trials, and hybrid models using product and go-to-market context.

faq.question: Can it plan a price increase?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers grandfathering, delayed rollout, plan restructuring, customer messaging, and measurement.

faq.question: Does it replace financial or legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides strategic guidance and should be reviewed by finance, legal, and customer-facing teams.
